context:
Case 42 is one fixed month, July 2026, of a small print and design studio's checking account. The data source is deterministic: the case number alone selects the statement and the books, so every call for this case returns the same data. The statement covers 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-31 and has 12 to 16 bank lines, each with an id, posting date, bank descriptor, amount, and a processor only for card-processor payouts, plus the card processors' fee rules. The books are the business's entries for the same month, each with an id, booking date, memo, vendor or customer, and amount. Start by reading both the statement and the books for case 42 in one step.

Match each bank line to the book entries it pays using the counterparty the texts name. Read the descriptor's merchant name, abbreviation or processor against each entry's vendor and memo: for example, AMZN MKTP US* is Amazon's store, SQ * is a shop paid through Square, and a payout whose processor is set pays the entries the books record as "paid by card, <that processor>". A MOBILE DEPOSIT pays a customer's check the books record as deposited; CHECK <number> pays the entry with that check number. Never match on amount and date alone: several entries share an amount and a date, and only the counterparty tells them apart.

Rules every reconciliation must satisfy: a bank line's date is 0 to 3 days after each entry it pays; its amount equals the sum of its entries' amounts, except for a processor payout, whose amount is each entry less that processor's fee (the stated percent of the payment rounded half up to the cent, plus the fixed part). Exactly one bank line in the case pays two entries; every other match pays one entry. Use every id exactly once: matched ids go in matches, and ids with no counterpart go in unmatched_bank if they are bank lines the books lack (bank fees, interest, autopays) or unmatched_books if they are book entries the bank lacks (uncleared checks, deposits or charges not on the statement). Amounts are in dollars to the cent, money in positive and money out negative. Identical charges at one merchant on one day booked as two entries are interchangeable, so either pairing of them counts as correct.

Save the complete reconciliation, and if the save refuses, fix exactly the problems it lists and save again. Submit exactly the summary returned by the last successful save.
